title: TSMC overseas fabs see profit flip in 1H26
author: user nl
text:
user nl
Well-known member

Arizona swings sharply into the black​Arizona's profitability has risen quickly, helped by tight demand for P1 capacity, higher foundry pricing, and gradually easing build-out costs.

Financial statements show the fab earned NT$4.728 billion(US$148.85 million) in the first half of 2025 and NT$16.141 billion for full-year 2025; in the first half of 2026, profit jumped to NT$36.066 billion, up about 663% from the first half of 2025. Because TSMC(2330.TW) owns 100% of the Arizona fab, it booked an investment gain of NT$31.151 billion in the first half of 2026.

Based on TSMC's roughly NT$1.28 trillion net profit in the first half of 2026, that investment gain accounted for about 2.44% of overall earnings.

Even so, Arizona's profit remains sensitive to the costs of continued expansion. TSMC booked an Arizona investment gain of about NT$14.603 billion in the second quarter of 2026, down about 13.6% from NT$16.909 billion in the first quarter, indicating that depreciation, amortization and operating costs from ongoing construction at P2 and other future sites will continue to pressure earnings.

........................................................................

Subsidy reliance fades as overseas earnings grow​TSMC's overseas earnings growth is also reducing its reliance on government subsidies. In 2025, TSMC received a combined NT$7.63 billion in government support from the US, Germany, Japan and China, but that fell to just NT$590 million in the first half of 2026.

Arizona's tax credit benefit has also increased. Investments that previously qualified for a credit equal to 25% of the investment amount will, under regulatory changes taking effect January 1, 2026, qualify for a 35% tax credit if they meet the conditions.
